identity: Arabic song lyric — the Arabic-dub opening theme of Digimon ("أبطال الديجيتال"). Scraped from a lyrics page: no punctuation survives at all, one sung phrase per line, a chorus block of nonsense vocables (لالالالا وووووو), a refrain repeated verbatim (نعلم أنا لن يعيدنا الأمل / من عالم الديجتال / بل العمل معا), and an uncorrected typo صدبق for صديق that marks the source as low-quality scrape.
law: Layout register, like §T comic balloons and §J worksheet lines: THE LINE IS THE UNIT. 83 tokens across 16 layout lines = 4.4 tokens per line, already far below the ~10-16 prose norm of LAW 0⁗, so the density argument that drove the batch-13 under-cutting correction gives me no licence to cut inside a line here. Free boundaries (token before every <NL>, plus the final token) are taken in full; nothing else.
reasoning:
Three internal sites tempted me and I welded all three.
(1) Line 1, @3 وقعنا: 'في فخ غريب وقعنا | في عالم الأرقام ضعنا' is two complete finite predications, each with its own fronted PP, which under LAW 0'' (default CUT at a fresh finite predication) and LAW 0''' item 9 (fronted adverbial attaches FORWARD, so the cut would go at @3, before في عالم) is the strongest cut candidate in the document. I weld it because LAW 0' is prior: a boundary is a mark in the SOURCE, and this source carries no marks. The two clauses were printed on one line; if the transcriber had heard two sentences he would have broken the line, as he did sixteen other times. The layout IS the punctuation in this document.
(2) Line 2, @10 and @12: 'كيف الخروج كيف الخروج من أين الطريق' — three questions. T8 says a question cuts only when it is a complete conversational turn; these are a repeated lyric cry, not turns, and LAW 3 as revised says asyndetic repetition welds unless each element was a complete printed sentence. It was not. Weld.
(3) Line 3, @19/@21: 'عالم غريب المعالم نواجه الأخطار نقاوم' — a bare NP topic followed by two asyndetic verbs sharing a subject. §P1 (short asyndetic clauses chain inside one sentence) and LAW 0''' item 2 (gapped coordination) both weld this.
Costing: at every one of these sites cutting-wrongly and welding-wrongly are exactly symmetric in F1 (one extra FP vs one extra FN against the same 16 true positives), so the decision is a pure probability call, and I put P(the lyrics page punctuated mid-line) well under 0.5. Result: 16 boundaries, all of them free ones, mean segment 5.2 tokens — the LAW 0⁗ sanity check passes without any prose-style cut.
